title: Quantum State Preparation Based on LimTDD
problem: Efficient quantum state preparation for complex quantum states requires better representations and circuit implementations.
motivation: Rapid advancement in quantum technologies demands efficient state preparation methods to improve quantum computing practicality.
method: LimTDD works by splitting quantum states into smaller, connected pieces using tensor networks—a mathematical way to break large states into factors. These pieces are then stored using decision diagrams, a tree-like structure that compactly represents them by skipping redundant branches. Because quantum states grow exponentially in size, this compact factorization allows the method to represent and work with states that would otherwise be too large to fit in memory.
key_novelty: Combining tensor networks with decision diagrams creates a more compact representation for quantum states.
contributions: Exponential efficiency gains over existing methods in best-case scenarios
Efficient representation of complex quantum states
Theoretical and practical foundation for quantum computing
limitations: Limited implementation details; best-case exponential gains may not generalize to all quantum states.
primary_theme: LimTDD for efficient quantum state preparation
